title: Senior Grant Writer
description:
Title: Senior Grant Writer

Dept/Program: Development

Reports to: Chief of Staff

Status: Full-time, Exempt

Salary Range: $75,000

Our Family Services is seeking an experienced Senior Grant Writer who can independently lead the development of complex, competitive grant applications with minimal supervision. The primary purpose of this position is to oversee all grant functions of the agency with support and input from the Chief of Staff and the Chief Executive Officer. This position reviews and applies for all government and private grant funding and coordinates submission of all grant reports as well as proper tracking of program outcomes.

The Senior Grant Writer, along with the Chief of Staff, coordinates resource development, grant writing, major gifts and planned giving, fundraising, special events, marketing, communications, and public relations to support the programs and staff to acquire and maintain the resources they need to provide quality services.

All agency positions are expected to meet the agency standards for attendance and punctuality, positive interactions with others, effective work habits, knowledge and skills, judgment and ethics. The successful candidate must be able to review and interpret funding opportunities, develop grant strategies, identify information gaps, conduct research, coordinate with clients and technical staff, develop project work plans and measurable outcomes, and produce comprehensive, submission-ready applications. We are looking for someone who is independent but highly collaborative, confident but open-minded, and experienced but willing to listen, learn, and adapt.

The specific expectations and essential duties of this position include:

  • Appreciates and supports the mission and goals of Our Family Services
  • Review NOFOs, RFAs, and other funding announcements.
  • Determine eligibility, application requirements, scoring criteria, deadlines, and documentation needs.
  • Develop grant strategies, application checklists, schedules, and information requests.
  • Creates and implements a realistic annual plan for the grants program to support the organization’s mission and goals, annual plan and budget.
  • Oversees all aspects of grant applications and reporting, including targeted sponsorship applications, within deadlines.
  • Creates realistic grant proposals that can be effectively implemented with the funding requested.
  • Creates sustainability and evaluation plans.
  • Creates budget narratives and justifications.
  • Researches and strategizes new funding opportunities.
  • Develops interesting and compelling ways to communicate the agency’s impact through narrative and infographics. Conduct research using credible federal, state, Tribal, academic, and other authoritative sources.
  • Facilitates meetings with program staff to acquire sufficient and accurate information to write successful grants.
  • Develops and maintains sustainable community engagement strategies and forms partnerships necessary to create competitive applications for funding and successful implementation of contracts.
  • Translate broad project concepts into clearly defined, competitive, and fundable proposals.
  • Identify weaknesses, missing information, or documentation and recommend solutions.
  • Coordinate with managers, clients, partners, technical staff, and subject matter experts.
  • Ensure consistency among narratives, budgets, schedules, and supporting documents.
  • Track forms, attachments, letters of support, certifications, and other application requirements.
  • Conduct quality-control and compliance reviews before submission.
  • Deliver polished, substantially submission-ready applications for final management review.
  • Develops and maintains relationships with private funders, in partnership with the Chief of Staff.
  • Manages site visits with current and potential funders.
  • Maintains and updates passwords, subscriptions, and enrollment in private grant-related external systems.
  • Creates and implements analysis protocols and regular reporting to the Chief of Staff and other key leaders regarding upcoming funding opportunities, current activities and rates of success for grants program.
  • Contributes content to the Annual Report, agency newsletter and other communications
  • Provides regular updates on progress and activities to the Chief of Staff.
  • Manages collection and reporting of agency outcomes data.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Expected Level of Independence

This is a senior-level position. After receiving a funding opportunity, project concept, and relevant background information, the successful candidate should be able to:

  • Develop the application strategy and structure.
  • Develop goals, objectives, activities, outcomes, and performance measures.
  • Draft comprehensive application narratives.
  • Identify application weaknesses and recommend improvements.
  • Produce a substantially complete, submission-ready application.

The candidate should know what questions to ask, what information is missing, and what needs to happen next without waiting for detailed instructions.

As this position is part of the agency’s Leader’s Group, the following leadership expectations also apply:

  • Upholds agency staff values and expectations
  • Engages in respectful and ongoing communication and problem-solving with others
  • Follows protocol and established procedures while still being creative and taking initiative to do what needs to be done
  • Acts as a positive and professional ambassador for the agency both internally and in the greater community
  • Takes all practical steps to ensure a work environment that is safe, friendly, helpful, and free from harassment
  • Successfully engages, coordinates, and motivates agency staff to achieve program or project goals
  • Is able to face adversity, take unpopular stands, or engage in tough debates when necessary, but knows when to move on

Collaboration and Teamwork

Our Family Services places a high value on teamwork. The successful candidate must be:

  • Open-minded and willing to consider different perspectives and approaches.
  • A strong team player who enjoys working collaboratively.
  • Respectful of clients, community members, technical professionals, and colleagues.
  • Comfortable receiving constructive feedback and revising work when needed.
  • Able to balance independent judgment with collaborative decision-making.
  • Flexible when project direction or funding requirements change.
  • Proactive in communicating questions, concerns, risks, and ideas.
  • Willing to support other team members when deadlines require additional help.
  • Focused on producing the best overall project and team result.
  • Takes ownership of an application without taking ownership away from the team.

title: Case Specialist RELS
description:
GENERAL FUNCTION:

Under the direction of the Owner, Executive Director and Program Administrator, the Case Specialist is responsible for supervising ILS/SLS/AST Educators in the implementation of Individual Service Plans (ISP) through the guidance of area Regional Centers, focusing on increasing consumer independence by providing independent living skills to adults with developmental disabilities. Case Specialist will support consumers as they receive services which supports their right to choice, independence, and self-empowerment while establishing realistic goal opportunities in the areas of self-care, public transportation, socialization and vocational exploration.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILIES:

  • Work collaboratively with ILS/SLS/AST Educators and Field Supervisors to identify and evaluate the development of specific and realistic consumer goals related to teaching independent living skills.
  • Preparing and implementing quality assurance policies and procedures and case management
  • Performing routine calls a minimum of 1x per month to active consumers; Calling consumers daily to ensure quality of service.
  • Communicate with appropriate department at Regional Center and provide updates on consumer progress.
  • Call consumers that are on hold to identify the status of their services.
  • Identify and ensure all active consumers have active authorizations.
  • Communicate with Intake & Scheduling Department regularly.
  • Update internal documentation platforms.
  • Work collaboratively with scheduling department to assign educators to new or existing consumer's and encourage

their active involvement in proper decision-making, problem-solving and conflict resolution.

  • Schedule educators for quarterly written evaluations of consumer's development and behavioral

interaction; review reports for accuracy and proper documentation.

  • Conduct functional assessments to in-coming consumers to establish realistic treatment programs that

effect the development of specific goals and objectives.

  • Submit Special Incident Reports within 24 hours; per requirement from Regional Center.
  • Complete Quality Assurance calls with employees mid month to ensure authorized hours are being completed.
  • Maintain active communication and provide feedback to ILS/SLS/AST Educators, Field Supervisors, and

  • RC Service Coordinator; represent company during IPP meetings and consumer assessments.

  • Advocate and work closely with consumer through governmental agencies such as Medi-Cal, AFDC, SSI,

  • IHSS and other non-profit organizations.

  • Identifying and resolving workflow and service issues.
  • Ensure authorized hours are being met each month
  • Addressing and discussing issues and proposed solutions with Executive Department.
  • Documenting quality assurance activities.
  • Making recommendations for improvement.
  • Creating training materials, as needed.

title: Corps Director of Development I (8569)
description:
LOCATION: Salisbury, Maryland Corps

POSITION: Corps Director of Development I

POSITION TYPE: full-time, exempt

PAY RATE: $61,000 - $65,000

This position is responsible for:

Creating and overseeing the implementation of a strategic approach to increase fundraising results through major gifts, corporate donations, grant solicitation, direct mail, special events, community relations and in-kind resources.

Key Responsibilities:

ANNUAL FUND DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES

  • By February 15th each year create a fund development plan in consultation with the Corps Officer and Divisional Development Director (DDD) that includes an individual goal for the development director and sets specific goals and strategies for appropriate development disciplines that will increase revenues to support the strategic direction of the organization; plan is submitted to the Corps Officer for approval and processing though the DDD for DFB for approval. Implement the approved fund development plan in accordance with ethical fundraising principles.
  • By the 15th of each month, evaluate and report to the Corps Officer on all fundraising activities to ensure that the fundraising goals are being achieved.
  • In collaboration with the Corps Officer develop and maintain the Community Relations & Development Committee, the Marketing and Public Relations Committee and the Bequest and Endowment Committee of the Advisory Board.
  • Actively support and cooperate with the divisional Planned Giving and Resource Development program representatives.
  • Monitor trends in the community or region and adapt fundraising strategies as necessary.
  • Cultivate existing funding resources and research and secure new funding opportunities for the command.
  • Manage and provide oversight over the three (3) major annual fundraising events (Golf tournament, Annual Dinner, and Kettle breakfast).

ORGANIZE FUND DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES

  • Develop and manage timelines for various fundraising activities to ensure strategic plans and critical fund-raising processes are carried out in a timely manner.
  • Develop procedures for the development department which reflect ethical fundraising practices.
  • Prepare and submit grant applications as outlined in the development plan.
  • Oversee the planning and execution of special fundraising events as specified in the development plan.
  • In cooperation with the Regional Resource Development Director and Corps Officer, identify and develop a personal portfolio of at least 20 corporate, community and/or individual prospects that will be put into a moves management system that the development director manages.
  • Meet or surpass an annual fundraising goal from major gift efforts that is established by the Corps Officer and approved by the Divisional Finance Board.
  • In cooperation with the Regional Resource Development Director, manage a portfolio of the top 10 prospects and donors for the Corps Officer’s involvement.
  • In cooperation with the Regional Planned Giving Director staff the Bequest and Endowment Committee of the Advisory Board.
  • Increase overall revenue on an annual basis as established in the annual fund-raising plan.
  • Oversee the administration of a donor mailing list and Inter-Change which respects the privacy and confidentiality of donor information.
  • Work with direct mail vendors on all aspects of direct mail, set up annual calendar of mailings, review appeals and ensure timely processing of approvals from the Corps Officer, provide monthly direct mail reports and provide analysis on the direct mail program.
  • Have a strong working knowledge of InterChange, personally enter the recording of all gifts and donor interactions in a timely and proper manner.
  • Manages the acknowledgement program to provide a high level of donor relations.
  • Coordinate in-kind donations and make decisions regarding the issuing of receipts.
  • Manage the United Way application process and follow up processes according to policy.

STAFF FUND DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES

  • Engage volunteers for special fund development projects using established volunteer management practices.
  • Assist the Corps Officer in staffing the Advisory Organizations.

MANAGE FUND DEVELOPMENT BUDGET

  • By February 15th each year develop and submit to the Corps Officer an annual revenue and expenditure budget for the fund development program.
  • Monitor expenses and analyze budget reports on fund development and recommend changes as necessary.

PUBLIC RELATIONS

  • Foster an understanding of philanthropy within the organization.
  • Develop a comprehensive communication and marketing plan to promote the organization and maximize public awareness of the fundraising activities of the organization and of the value of Family Thrift Store.
  • Coordinate the design, printing and distribution of marketing and communication materials for development efforts in accordance with the communications and marketing plan.
  • Produce an annual report by February 15th of each year.
  • Build relationships with community stakeholders to advance the mission and fundraising goals of the organization.
  • Produce and distribute a minimum of 12 press releases in accordance with the communications and marketing plan.
  • Manage the Corps website and social media program.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS AND WORKING CONDITIONS

  • Limited amount of physical effort required associated with walking, standing, lifting, and carrying light objects (less than 25 lbs.).
  • Work may be performed in an office environment where there are little or no physical discomforts associated with changes in weather or discomforts associated with noise, dust, dirt, and the like but not limited to the office environment.

Employee Benefits:

  • Paid Time Off
  • Retirement Savings Plan Available
  • Supplemental Insurance Available
  • Voluntary Life Insurance and more!

title: Librarian
description:
Librarian

Location: Austin Christian University, Georgetown, TX

Reports to: Provost

Summary of Role

The Librarian supports the academic mission of Austin Christian University by providing professional oversight of library resources, research services, and information systems. This role ensures students and faculty have access to relevant, academically rigorous resources that support the University’s curriculum and Christian mission.

Working collaboratively with faculty and university leadership, the Librarian manages collection development, provides advanced research and reference support, strengthens student information literacy, and maintains effective cataloging and library systems. The Librarian also helps anticipate evolving academic resource needs, evaluates resource utilization, and ensures library practices align with applicable accreditation, academic, and regulatory standards.

Position Status & Schedule

  • Non-exempt
  • Hourly
  • Part-time (25 hours per week)
  • Schedule varies based on academic calendar, institutional priorities, and key university events; may include evenings and weekends
  • University events (i.e. Welcome Week, Graduation) and academic milestones will require availability outside of standard business hours
  • Easter/Christmas services and WAVE Student Conference are required workdays for this position

Essential Functions & Responsibilities

Collection Development & Management

  • Evaluate and maintain physical and digital library collections to ensure academic rigor, relevance, and theological alignment with the University’s curriculum and Christian mission.
  • Propose new resource acquisitions based on curriculum needs, faculty input, and emerging academic priorities.
  • Manage the ongoing review and de-selection of outdated, duplicative, or no longer relevant materials.

Reference & Academic Support

  • Provide advanced, customized reference support for students and faculty.
  • Assist faculty in identifying scholarly materials for course development and integration.
  • Coordinate with faculty subject-matter experts to create and manage specialized subject guides (LibGuides) supporting theology, ministry, business, and general education courses.

Information Literacy

  • Design and deliver instructional sessions on academic research methods, including new and emerging research technologies.
  • Equip students to critically evaluate sources and effectively navigate academic databases.
  • Develop asynchronous learning materials (tutorials, handouts) for different learning modalities.

Cataloging & Systems

  • Perform original and complex copy cataloging using current metadata standards (RDA, MARC).
  • Maintain accurate classification and organization of theological and academic texts.
  • Maintain and troubleshoot library management systems and academic database access to support reliable use by students and faculty.

Strategic Administration

  • Partner with faculty and University departments to anticipate and plan for upcoming academic resource needs.
  • Track and evaluate library resource usage to inform collection development and future budget decisions.
  • Ensure library practices comply with applicable academic accreditation and approval standards and federal and state requirements.

Contributes to the overall success of the University by performing other duties as assigned

Requirements

  • Strong commitment to Christian faith and ability to lead in alignment with the University’s Statement of Faith and Standards of Performance.
  • Uphold the Core Values of the University, exemplifying them by word and lifestyle.
  • Participate in the social, cultural, and spiritual life of the University community, including regular Chapel attendance.
  • Support the educational purposes and objectives of the University
  • Proven ability to lead through complexity, manage change, and improve academic and student outcomes.
  • Cooperate with the administration and staff of the University in professional and personal relationships.
  • Observe and enforce the rules and regulations of the University.
  • Support the University prayerfully on a regular basis.
  • Ability to work evenings/weekends as needed for academic events and crises.
  • Travel for accreditation, partnerships, and conferences as required.
  • Successful completion of background check, driver record, and reference checks.
  • Be an active Member of Celebration Church.
  • Regularly attend services at Celebration Church.
  • Tithe faithfully and regularly to Celebration Church.
  • Abide by the values, policies, and practices within the Celebration Church Employee Handbook.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience
  • Minimum 3 years of library science or related professional experience
  • MLS/MLIS or related advanced degree preferred
  • Prior experience in a higher education or academic library setting preferred

Competencies

  • Demonstrated passion for and alignment with the mission, values, and vision of Austin Christian University
  • Demonstrates depth of knowledge in library science, academic research, information literacy, collection stewardship, and evolving library technologies.
  • Exercises sound independent judgment when navigating academic needs, resource decisions, and competing priorities.
  • Understands the connection between library resources, curriculum, faculty needs, and student learning and applies that perspective to thoughtful decision-making.
  • Demonstrates strong research acumen and the ability to effectively navigate, evaluate, organize, and communicate scholarly information.
  • Maintains a high standard of accuracy, organization, and consistency when working with academic resources, information systems, classification, and data.
  • Builds productive relationships across faculty, staff, students, and University leadership through professionalism, responsiveness, and a collaborative approach.
  • Approaches challenges with curiosity and resourcefulness, independently identifying solutions and opportunities for improvement.
  • Remains current in evolving academic practices, technologies, accreditation expectations, and library standards and readily adapts to changing University needs.
  • Demonstrates thoughtful stewardship of University resources, balancing academic quality, institutional priorities, utilization, and long-term needs.
  • Approaches students, faculty, and the broader University community with responsiveness, professionalism, and a commitment to supporting teaching, research, and learning.
  • Builds trust and credibility through subject-matter expertise, sound judgment, reliability, professionalism, and consistent follow-through.

Work Environment & Physical Demands

  • Primarily works in an air-conditioned office environment with adequate lighting and moderate noise levels
  • No hazardous or significantly unpleasant working conditions
  • Ability to remain in a stationary position approximately 50% of the time
  • Ability to move about University and Church facilities as needed
  • Regular use of computers, phones, and standard office equipment; ability to talk and hear
  • Frequent standing, walking, sitting, and use of hands and arms to handle files and equipment
  • Ability to reach, stoop, crouch, kneel, and access supplies on lower shelves or in storage areas
  • Frequent repetitive hand, wrist, and finger movements
  • Ability to occasionally lift and/or move items weighing up to 20 pounds
  • Vision abilities required include close, distance, peripheral, and color vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus
  • Moderate exposure to physical risk
  • Ability to perform the essential duties of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation; employees requiring accommodation must notify their supervisor or Human Resources

Other Information

Celebration Church, which includes Austin Christian University, is an equal employment opportunity employer to the extent required by law applicable to religious institutions.

The statements in this job description are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed and are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, or tasks. Other duties, responsibilities, and activities may be assigned at any time, with or without notice. This job description is not intended to create, and does not constitute, an employment contract. Austin Christian University maintains its status as an at-will employer, and employment may be terminated by either party at any time for any reason not prohibited by law.

title: Mental Health Professional (4298)
description:
About Us

National Counseling Group has been the most trusted provider for Home-Based and Community services in Virginia since 1993. Through the years, our dedication to excellence, results and innovation has resulted in becoming the leading provider for mental, behavioral, and substance use services.

Our dedication to the individuals we serve and the communities in which they live is the foundation for everything we do. With passionate and knowledge staff, we are able to make an impact with individuals who need it most.

About the Role


As a Mental Health Professional, you will:

  • Case Management & Documentation: Maintain accurate and timely case records per licensing and Medicaid standards, ensuring continuity and quality of care.
  • Crisis Intervention: Provide direct support during crisis situations, helping clients to navigate and stabilize through effective case management.
  • Service Planning & Coordination: Coordinate and develop Individualized Service Plans with input from team members and stakeholders to align treatment goals.
  • Trauma-Informed Counseling: Deliver person-centered, trauma-informed, and psycho-educational interventions designed to support treatment objectives.

description:
The Communications Specialist 4 will support a major, multi-year business transformation initiative at Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL). This position will lead strategic and tactical communications supporting the implementation of a modern enterprise resource planning (ERP) platform, replacing legacy business systems with SAP S/4HANA and integrated applications.

Working closely with program leadership, change management, functional workstreams, system integration partners, and other stakeholders, the Communications Specialist will develop and execute communications strategies designed to keep employees informed, engaged, and prepared throughout the transformation.

Key responsibilities include:

• Develop and execute strategic communication plans supporting a large-scale, enterprise-wide business transformation.

• Partner with program leadership, change management teams, workstream leads, system integrators, and internal stakeholders to identify communication needs and develop effective messaging.

• Create, write, edit, and manage communications for employees, managers, executives, and other stakeholder groups.

• Develop content across multiple communication channels, including newsletters, web content, presentations, executive communications, announcements, correspondence, and multimedia materials.

• Maintain consistent messaging across the program and ensure communications are clear, timely, accurate, and aligned with project objectives.

• Translate complex technical, business, and organizational changes into understandable communications for diverse audiences.

• Support organizational change management efforts by communicating how upcoming changes will affect employees and what resources, training, and support will be available.

• Develop executive-level communications and effectively capture the voice and messaging style of senior leadership.

• Coordinate with multimedia professionals to strategically incorporate graphics, photography, video, and other visual content into communication campaigns.

• Support communications across multiple functional workstreams while managing competing priorities and deadlines.

• Establish and maintain communication protocols, processes, and standards across the program team.

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams and internal partner organizations to support employee engagement and adoption of new business processes and systems.

This is a hybrid position supporting Los Alamos and Santa Fe, New Mexico. The selected candidate must reside within approximately two hours' ground commute of the work location. Work arrangements are subject to management discretion and may change based on program needs.

title: Aquatics Professional

description:
SWIM INSTRUCTOR — LITTLE KICKERS SWIM SCHOOL

Reports To

Aquatics Director

Compensation

$20 – $50 / hour (based on tier level)

Employment Type

Part-Time or Full-Time Hourly

ABOUT THIS ROLE

Little Kickers Swim School is not your average swim school, and this is not your average swim instructor job. We are a team of passionate, career-minded people who are changing what aquatics looks like. We hold ourselves to a world-class standard, we invest deeply in our instructors, and we protect our culture fiercely. If you are looking for a place to clock in and clock out, this is not it. If you are looking for a place to build something real, grow, and be part of a team that genuinely cares, keep reading.

We are selective. We hire people who want to be here for the long haul, who take pride in what they do, and who understand that what we do matters. Our families trust us with their most precious people, and we take that seriously every single day.

We run a five-tier instructor advancement system, with our top Tier 5 instructors earning up to $50/hour. From your very first shift, you are on a path to grow. We invest in you because we believe great swim instruction is a career, not a side job.

COMPENSATION & GROWTH

  • Starting Pay: $25/hour from day one
  • 60-Day Review: Opportunity to earn up to $32/hour based on performance
  • Bi-Annual Reviews: Structured reviews with a clear level system and transparent path for advancement

BENEFITS

  • Medical, Dental & Vision Insurance: For employees working 30+ hours per week (our full-time threshold)
  • 401(k): auto-enrolled with company matching after 6 months of hire.
  • PTO & Sick Time

NON-NEGOTIABLE REQUIREMENTS

Please do not apply if you do not meet all of the following:

  • Comfort and confidence in the water, you must be a strong, capable swimmer
  • Genuine passion for working with children from five months old through school age
  • Comfort working independently with infants and young children. Parents do not enter the water at Little Kickers, even with our youngest swimmers. You must be confident holding, supporting, and instructing babies and toddlers on your own
  • Reliable, consistent availability. Our kids build trust with their instructors, and our families count on you being there
  • Strong communication skills with both children and parents
  • A career mindset, we are looking for people who want to grow with us, not just fill a shift

OUR CULTURE — YOU MUST LIVE THESE

At Little Kickers, our core values are not wall art. They are how we hire, how we coach, and how we hold each other accountable. This role requires someone who does not just understand these values, but embodies them:

🎉 Have Freakin’ Fun

Energy is contagious. You bring it every single lesson.

💪 Sweat

You work hard. You are in the water. You lead by example.

🌟 World Class Service

Every family. Every class. Every time.

🪨 Be Rock Solid

Reliable. Consistent. Your kids can count on you.

🤝 Build Connections

With students, families, and your fellow instructors.

📚 Learn, Improve, Grow

You are never done getting better. Neither are your students.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

Instruction — This Is the Heart of the Role

You will deliver private, one-on-one swim lessons to children ranging from five months old through swim team level. This is focused, intentional, high-quality instruction that makes a real difference in a child's life. Parents cheer from the viewing gallery while you own the water. No parents in the pool. Ever. From day one, you are the one building trust, providing comfort, and creating a safe and joyful experience for every single child in your lane.

  • Conduct engaging, structured private lessons for children of all ages and skill levels
  • Independently support and instruct infants and young children without parents in the water, confidence with babies is a must
  • Follow the Little Kickers curriculum and five-tier instructional framework
  • Assess each swimmer and tailor instruction to meet them exactly where they are
  • Provide real-time feedback and encouragement that builds genuine confidence
  • Adapt your approach to accommodate different skill levels, learning paces, and abilities
  • Create a fun, supportive environment where kids feel safe to try, fail, and grow

Safety and Supervision

Safety is non-negotiable. Full stop. Every child in your lane is your responsibility, and you treat it that way.

  • Maintain constant vigilance and active supervision during every lesson
  • Enforce safety rules, pool protocols, and emergency procedures without exception
  • Ensure proper use of pool equipment and immediate response to any safety concern

Parent and Family Communication

Families trust us with their most precious people. Your communication after every lesson is a direct reflection of our world class standard.

  • Provide consistent, meaningful updates to parents and guardians on their child's progress after every lesson
  • Communicate achievements, areas for growth, and next steps with warmth and clarity
  • Coordinate with fellow instructors, front of house staff, and management to ensure consistency across the team

Professional Development

We are building career-track instructors, not part-time pool staff. We expect that same investment back from you.

  • Attend and actively participate in staff meetings and trainings
  • Complete required certification courses and stay current on safety protocols
  • Pursue advancement through our five-tier instructor system with the support of your Aquatics Director
  • Embrace feedback, coaching, and continuous improvement as a core part of the job

National Counseling Group has been the most trusted provider for Home-Based and Community services in Virginia since 1993. Through the years, our dedication to excellence, results and innovation has resulted in becoming the leading provider for mental, behavioral, and substance use services.
​
Our dedication to the individuals we serve and the communities in which they live is the foundation for everything we do. With passionate and knowledge staff, we are able to make an impact with individuals who need it most.

About the Role

Are you a compassionate and dedicated mental health professional looking to make a meaningful impact? National Counseling Group (NCG), is seeking a Functional Family Therapist (FFT) to join our team. In this role, you will work directly with youth and their families to address challenging behaviors through a structured, evidence-based treatment model. You will conduct comprehensive assessments, engage families in active, change-oriented therapy, and implement individualized treatment plans focused on achieving meaningful outcomes. Carrying a caseload of 10–12 clients, you will collaborate closely with families and community systems to build trust, ensure engagement, and support long-term success. Your work will include maintaining clear documentation aligned with the FFT model, participating in supervision and training, and delivering direct clinical services that make a tangible difference in the lives of those you serve. This is a unique opportunity to be part of a supportive, mission-driven team while developing your expertise in a proven therapeutic approach.

As a Functional Family Therapist, you will provide:

  • Conduct a comprehensive initial assessment to include all desired treatment outcomes, assessment of systemic strengths and needs, comprehensive safety plan, and analysis of contributing factors to referral behaviors
  • Carry a caseload of 10-12 clients
  • Engage the entire family unit in active change-oriented treatment by identifying and overcoming barriers to engagement
  • Implement problem conceptualization, treatment planning, intervention implementation, case outcome review, and strategy revision procedure
  • Maintain clear and concise documentation of treatment efforts that promote peer and supervisory review and feedback, and that demonstrate compliance with the FFT model
  • Collaborate with all relevant systems and key participants within each system to ensure their buy-in and cooperation throughout FFT treatment

POSITION PURPOSE: The CNA is responsible for providing residents with the highest quality of direct routine care in all activities of daily living, under the supervision of the LPN or RN and in accordance with the Nursing Assistant Program standards, the Resident’s Bill of Rights and the facility Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement (QAPI) program. According to the Plan of Care for the resident, CNAs apply skills in basic nursing, personal care and basic restorative services while understanding the mental health and social service needs of the resident and being mindful of the needs in cognitively impaired residents. The CNA is part of the interdisciplinary care team that is dedicated to promoting independence, autonomous decision-making and facilitating residents to achieve and maintain the highest practicable physical mental and psychosocial well-being.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS OF POSITION:

QUALITY OF CARE

  • Provides ongoing resident care upholding and promoting the resident’s right to be free from abuse, mistreatment, neglect, or misappropriation of resident property, immediately reporting any suspicions, reports or witnessed events to appropriate facility staff.
  • Forms quality relationships, communicating and interacting competently on a one-to-one basis while integrating the resident-centered Plan of Care
  • Demonstrates sensitivity to physical, mental, and psychosocial needs as well as maintaining dignity, while skillfully performing directed nursing, personal cares and restorative services
  • Supports and promotes residents’ rights and attainment of as much functional independence as possible.
  • Maximizes quality of living through continual monitoring and reporting of resident care, ensuring all outcomes are thoroughly and accurately documented.
  • Provides the highest quality care to all residents, without regard to race, gender, sexual orientation, religion, age or differences in culture.
  • Maintains awareness of facility QAPI goals and abides by and promotes the QAPI program.
  • Practices and promotes a strong culture of customer service, ensuring a resident-centered experience.

BASIC NURSING, PERSONAL CARES AND BASIC RESTORATIVE SERVICES

  • Facilitates Plan of Care through completion of nursing responsibilities, clearly communicating resident needs to primary caregivers and reporting changes and responses to interventions to the LPN or RN
  • Completes basic nursing cares as directed such as taking and recording vital signs; measuring and recording height and weight; recognizing abnormal changes in body functioning and reporting to the LPN or RN; and caring for resident who are actively dying.
  • Completes personal care as directed such as bathing; grooming; mouth care; dressing; toileting; eating and hydration; proper feeding techniques; skin care; and transfers, positioning and turning.
  • Facilitates adequate nutritional intake for resident through assisting to and from the dining area; feeding or assisting to feed; monitoring and recording intake and output; passing water and offering fluids; passing and collecting trays; serving supplemental nourishment as directed by nurse; maintaining awareness of dietary restrictions; and following safety guidelines including wearing gloves when handling food or hydration.
  • Completes basic restorative services as directed such as training residents in self-care and according to the resident’s abilities; use of assistive devices in transferring, ambulation, eating, and dressing; maintenance of range of motion; proper turning and positioning in bed and chair bowel and bladder training; and care and use of prosthetic and orthotic devices.
  • Assist nurses with special procedures as directed, including implementing and completing critical care sheets, participating in care conferences, etc.
  • Provides and ensures nursing care activities are practiced in accordance with Nursing Assistant Program standards while protecting residents’ dignity, privacy, and autonomous decision-making whenever possible.
  • Facilitates assistance in areas such as getting to and participating in activities as well as assistance in resolving any grievances or disputes.
  • Articulates meaningful discussion with residents based on their unique backgrounds, likes and dislikes.
  • Maintains care and security of residents’ personal possessions.
  • Interact with resident’s family or support network, visitors and members of the interdisciplinary care team in a courteous and cooperative manner.
  • Recognizes limits of knowledge, skill and experience; facilitates situations beyond the CNAs competency.

COMPLIANCE – SAFETY, DOCUMENTATION, HIPAA

  • Ensures all call lights are promptly and courteously answered.
  • Uses proper body mechanics at all times and reminds other nursing staff or facilitates correction.
  • Constantly adheres to safety policies and procedures in lifting, positioning and equipment use, including use of transfer belts, Hoyer or mechanical lifts.
  • Strictly follows Standard Precaution infection control procedures and OSHA guidelines regarding bloodborne pathogens to provide safe nursing care to include proper handwashing; maintaining disinfection/cleaning schedules; wearing PPE such as gloves, face shield, fluid resistant gowns, etc.
  • Maintains a safe, clean environment in resident rooms and facility following infection control procedures to bag infectious linens and equipment or proper disposal of them; proper handwashing, disinfection/cleaning schedules.
  • Avoids the need for restraints in accordance with DHS nursing home standards.
  • Ensures all cares are documented and that resident records are complete through systematic collection, reporting and documentation of data that is secure from unauthorized access and follows state and federal regulations, including HIPAA to ensure privacy and maintain confidentiality.
  • Promptly reports and documents incidents and errors involving residents, staff, visitors or self.
  • Prioritizes work assignments consistent with number and level of staff available and resident care acuity.
  • Reviews, departing staff report at start of shift, ensures duties and delegated tasks are complete at end of shift and reports off to nurse when leaving.

title: Cardiac Technician
description:
Cardiac Technician will provide bedside electrocardiograms (EKG/ECG), holter monitors and Dexa Scans to all Express Mobile Diagnostic Services, LLC (Express) patients. These patients can reside in long-term care facilities, correctional facilities, resident homes, personal care homes etc. Will complete diagnostic exams in a professional and timely manner. Cardiac Tech. will be provided with all overhead including Company Vehicle, Diagnostic Equipment, Fuel/Gas Card and all other necessary tools to complete exams. Cardiac Technician will interact with our Call Center Dispatch Department when necessary to report cases that are completed and will get exams from the “board” on our electronic system, Rapid Radiology where orders are housed.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • The tech. will call and schedule appointment visits, documenting all communication within the company software systems, along with any follow up information sought/obtained.
  • Job requires tech to travel in a company vehicle to multiple locations; this entails the need for tech to monitor vehicle condition, fuel consumption, necessary “upkeep” (oil changes, tire rotations etc.) and communicate all vehicle activities with any other staff using the vehicle through company provided vehicle logs.
  • Job requires tech to use several different pieces of equipment, all of which require care/upkeep and general maintenance.
  • Electrocardiograms (EKG/ECG) involve application of multiple electrode patches to patient body, inputting patient information, running machine application to receive electric printout of heart rhythm/function and uploading/emailing/copying results to ordering providers.
  • Holter monitors involve electrode application, obtaining a small patient history, explanation of the 24 hours of being “hooked up” to the monitor and the diary patient has to record any “episodes” that happen during that time frame. Tech must either coordinate with another employee or arrange to go back themselves once 24-hour period is complete to remove and retrieve device. Holter information is uploaded at the office via a desktop computer and sent off for reading.
  • Bone densitometer scans (DEXA) are obtained with a portable sonographic densitometer, small patient history obtained, results are uploaded/emailed/faxed appropriately, same as EKG’s.
  • Flexible to working any shift necessary including some weekends, evenings when necessary.
  • Follow company protocols with extreme attention to detail.
  • Respond to duties as directed by Area Supervisor and/or corporate personnel team members.

description:

Our dedication to the individuals we serve and the communities in which they live is the foundation for everything we do. With passionate and knowledge staff, we are able to make an impact with individuals who need it most.

title: Filling Technician
location: Tnemec North Kansas City - NORTH KANSAS CITY, MO 64116
description:
Position Summary

The Filling Technician is responsible for the safe, accurate, and efficient filling, packaging, labeling, and preparation of finished coating products for distribution. This position plays a critical role in ensuring that finished products meet Tnemec's quality, packaging, labeling, and customer requirements.

The Filling Technician operates filling and packaging equipment, verifies product and packaging information, performs routine quality checks, maintains accurate production documentation, and works as part of the manufacturing team to achieve daily production goals.

Success in this position requires strong attention to detail, dependability, commitment to safety and quality, and the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

Entry Level candidates that successfully complete all training and requirements can progress to $23.00 per hour in the first year.

Benefits Include:

9 Paid Holidays

88 hours of PTO in Year 1

Yearly Profit Sharing Bonus

Excellent Benefits Package including 401k, Health, Dental, Vision

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Filling & Packaging Operations

  • Operate filling, packaging, labeling, and related production equipment safely and efficiently.
  • Fill finished coatings and related products into designated containers according to established work instructions and production requirements.
  • Verify the correct product, container size, label, lid, packaging materials, and quantity before beginning each filling operation.
  • Monitor filling equipment to ensure proper fill weights and consistent product flow.
  • Properly seal, label, package, palletize, and prepare finished products for movement to inventory or distribution.
  • Change over filling equipment between products, container sizes, and production runs.
  • Perform routine equipment adjustments within established operating procedures.
  • Assist with equipment setup, cleaning, and sanitation between production runs.
  • Maintain an organized flow of materials throughout the filling and packaging process.

Quality Responsibilities

  • Verify product identification against batch tickets, filling instructions, and production documentation before filling begins.
  • Confirm labels accurately match the product, batch number, container size, and other required information.
  • Perform required fill-weight checks and document results.
  • Visually inspect finished containers for defects including:
    • Incorrect or damaged labels
    • Improperly applied labels
    • Damaged containers
    • Improper seals or lids
    • Paint or coating residue on containers
    • Incorrect fill levels
    • Packaging defects
  • Immediately stop or escalate the process when a potential quality issue is identified.
  • Segregate questionable or nonconforming material according to established procedures.
  • Complete required production and quality documentation accurately and timely.
  • Support the company's goal of producing quality product correctly the first time.

Safety Responsibilities

  • Perform all work in accordance with company safety policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.
  • Wear required personal protective equipment at all times.
  • Safely work around coatings, solvents, chemicals, industrial equipment, forklifts, and other manufacturing hazards.
  • Understand and follow chemical labeling, Safety Data Sheet, and hazardous-material handling requirements.
  • Immediately report unsafe conditions, spills, equipment problems, injuries, and near misses.
  • Follow established procedures for spill prevention, containment, and cleanup.
  • Participate in safety meetings, training, inspections, and continuous safety improvement activities.
  • Maintain awareness of pedestrian and powered industrial truck traffic within the manufacturing environment.

Equipment & Operational Responsibilities

  • Perform routine pre-operational inspections of assigned equipment.
  • Identify equipment abnormalities and communicate problems promptly to supervision or Maintenance.
  • Perform basic troubleshooting and adjustments within the scope of established training.
  • Assist with equipment changeovers and production line setup.
  • Follow lockout/tagout and equipment safety requirements when applicable.
  • Protect equipment from unnecessary damage and immediately report maintenance concerns.
  • Support efforts to reduce equipment downtime and improve production efficiency.

Productivity & Continuous Improvement

  • Work to achieve established production and filling expectations while maintaining safety and quality standards.
  • Minimize product loss, packaging waste, rework, and unnecessary downtime.
  • Participate in Lean Manufacturing, 5S, and continuous improvement activities.
  • Identify opportunities to improve workplace organization, safety, quality, and efficiency.
  • Maintain a clean and organized work area throughout the shift.
  • Participate in production meetings and communicate issues that may impact schedule attainment.
  • Assist other production areas when necessary and qualified.

Documentation & Accountability

  • Accurately complete production records, quality checks, inventory transactions, and other required documentation.
  • Follow established standard operating procedures and work instructions.
  • Maintain accurate product and batch traceability.
  • Immediately communicate production discrepancies or documentation errors.
  • Take ownership for the accuracy and quality of work performed.
  • Maintain consistent attendance and punctuality to support production requirements.

title: General Application
description:
Diablo Country Club is a historic club nestled at the foot of Mt. Diablo in the rolling hills of the East Bay region of San Francisco, CA. The historic Diablo Country Club, a "Century Old Gem of the Valley" was established in May 1914. Part of a large land parcel purchased by developer Robert Noble Burgess in 1912, it was known as the Oakwood Park Stock Farm stretching over 6,000 acres from Green Valley Road to Mount Diablo's peak. The grassy knolls and woodsy terrain was home to thoroughbred trotters, contentedly grazing alongside cattle herds in the shadow of Mount Diablo. A eucalyptus stand bordered the raceway and horse feed was sheltered in Swiss chalet barns in the shade of heritage oaks and rocky outcrops. Crops of hay, wheat, barley and alfalfa grew near the fruit orchards.

The legendary Diablo Country Club that today occupies 115 acres, part of the 6,000-acre Oakwood Park Farm, was previously on a land mass parcel that encompassed 50,000 acres from Diablo and Green Valley Roads to the mountain peak, clear across to where the Blackhawk Development is today. The club has been serving its membership for over 100 years and enjoys the unique attribute as California's original family oriented golf club. Excellence and sportsmanship for generations of members have stood the test of time. The grounds, originally an 1874 country estate for the families of railroad barons and gold mining icons, was converted in 1914 to a world class golf and country club by the founder Robert Noble Burgess. His vision to create "A Community with an Ideal" is evidenced in many of the structures and activities that exist to this day. From refreshments in the Carriage Lounge, circa 1881, to youth swim competition since 1914, entertaining in the Red Horse Tavern, Est. 1917 or a round of golf on the iconic 18-hole golf course designed by legends Jack Neville and William Watson, Diablo Country Club continues its tradition of being a welcoming place for their members and guests.

Diablo Country Club offers the finest in state of the art amenities including: a championship tennis facility which includes a separate tennis clubhouse; a competition swimming pool complex with a large deck for social activities; a full-service fitness center; two bocce ball courts; two restaurants and a ballroom that seats up to 400 people.

POSITION SUMMARY

Provide the highest level of quality and service to our guests in an incredibly friendly atmosphere. Assist servers in food service and restaurant cleanliness. Deliver food items from the kitchen to the guests' table in a timely manner.
